title: lib
summary: MSUI now follows current Benilla's complete bounded realmd orchestration: credentials normalize before the first socket, an ambiguous fixed-width server public key B is abandoned before proof and redialed on a fresh connection up to eight times, the eighth challenge is retained as the non-invented fallback, client-generated A/S/K/M1 values redraw under the matching encoding-stability guards, and only the retained socket proceeds through proof verification and realm-list fetch.

openItems.text: Ambiguous-B redial: Benilla redials the logon challenge (up to 8 times) when the server's SRP6 public key B is not width-stable (~1 in 137 dials), because those handshakes can fail proof verification despite a correct password; MSUI's RealmClient.Logon dials exactly once, so roughly 0.7% of logons can spuriously reject a correct password
openItems.resolution: 2026-08-22: RealmLogonLaw owns the exact high-order-byte stability predicate, eight-dial bound, and final-dial fallback. RealmClient abandons ambiguous challenges before proof and disposes each rejected socket; Srp6Client also carries current Benilla's bounded A/S/K/M1 redraw guards. The isolated focused and full clinical suites pass without making a network connection.

openItems.text: Live-verify a normal authenticated realmd login and, with an owner-operated controlled challenge fixture if one is available, confirm an ambiguous B closes before proof and the following stable challenge succeeds without a spurious 0x04.
